items.title: A functor commuting with countable products commutes with derived limits
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file injectives.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that an additive functor from a Grothendieck abelian category to an abelian category with exact countable products, commuting with countable products, has a derived functor commuting with derived limits (statement lines 2282-2293). The proof is a complete argument: the derived functor exists by the existence of K-injective resolutions (proof lines 2295-2300); it is computed by evaluating on a K-injective representative, and products in the derived category are computed termwise, so the commutation with countable products passes to the derived level (proof lines 2300-2312); and the two descriptions together give the assertion (proof lines 2312-2316). The non-formal content is the comparison of the two computations of the product. The claim is H2.
